issues.description: SQL injection vulnerability in searchTodos function. The keyword parameter is directly interpolated into the SQL query using template literals without parameterization. An attacker can inject malicious SQL by passing inputs like "'; DROP TABLE todos; --" to execute arbitrary SQL commands.
issues.suggestion: Use parameterized queries: const query = 'SELECT * FROM todos WHERE title LIKE $1 OR description LIKE $1'; const rows = await db.query(query, [`%${keyword}%`]);

issues.description: SQL injection vulnerability in searchTodosByStatus function. The completed parameter is concatenated directly into the SQL query without validation or parameterization. An attacker can inject SQL commands like "true; DROP TABLE todos; --" to compromise the database.
issues.suggestion: Use parameterized queries: const sql = 'SELECT * FROM todos WHERE completed = $1'; const rows = await db.query(sql, [completed]);

issues.description: SQL injection vulnerability in getTodosByUser function. The userId parameter is interpolated into the SQL query using template literals without parameterization. An attacker can inject SQL such as "1' OR '1'='1" to bypass authentication or "1'; DROP TABLE user_todos; --" to execute destructive commands.
issues.suggestion: Use parameterized queries: const query = 'SELECT t.* FROM todos t JOIN user_todos ut ON t.id = ut.todo_id WHERE ut.user_id = $1'; const rows = await db.query(query, [userId]);

issues.description: Type mismatch in searchTodosByStatus function. The completed parameter is typed as string but should be boolean to match the Todo interface's completed field. This will cause runtime errors when the database expects a boolean value, and allows invalid string inputs that cannot be converted to boolean.
issues.suggestion: Change the parameter type to boolean: export async function searchTodosByStatus(completed: boolean): Promise<Todo[]>

issues.description: Missing input validation in searchTodos function. Unlike existing functions (createTodo validates and sanitizes inputs), searchTodos does not validate the keyword parameter for empty strings, excessive length, or malicious patterns before use.
issues.suggestion: Add input validation: if (!keyword || keyword.trim().length === 0) { return []; } if (keyword.length > 100) { throw new Error('Search keyword too long'); }

issues.description: Missing input validation in getTodosByUser function. The userId parameter is not validated for format, length, or empty values before database query execution, inconsistent with the validation patterns used in createTodo.
issues.suggestion: Add input validation: if (!userId || userId.trim().length === 0) { throw new Error('Invalid user ID'); }

issues.description: Missing input validation in searchTodosByStatus function. No validation ensures the completed parameter is a valid boolean value before database query execution.
issues.suggestion: Add validation: if (typeof completed !== 'boolean') { throw new Error('Invalid completed status'); }

issues.description: Inefficient LIKE pattern in searchTodos. The leading wildcard '%keyword%' pattern prevents the database from using indexes effectively, resulting in full table scans. For large todo lists, this will cause significant performance degradation.
issues.suggestion: Consider using full-text search capabilities (e.g., PostgreSQL's tsvector/tsquery) for better performance, or if prefix matching is acceptable, use 'keyword%' instead of '%keyword%' to allow index usage.

issues.description: Inconsistent error handling in searchTodos. The function does not handle the case where db.query might throw an error, unlike the defensive patterns that should be established in a production codebase. Additionally, it returns an empty-looking result on error instead of propagating the error.
issues.suggestion: Add explicit error handling: try { const rows = await db.query(query, params); return rows as Todo[]; } catch (error) { throw new Error(`Failed to search todos: ${error.message}`); }

issues.description: Type assertion 'as Todo[]' bypasses TypeScript's type checking without runtime validation. The database might return data that doesn't match the Todo interface (e.g., missing fields, wrong types), which would cause runtime errors downstream.
issues.suggestion: Consider adding runtime validation: return rows.map(row => ({ id: row.id, title: row.title, description: row.description, completed: Boolean(row.completed), createdAt: new Date(row.created_at) }));

codeQuality.summary: Critical security vulnerabilities detected: All three new functions (searchTodos, searchTodosByStatus, getTodosByUser) contain SQL injection vulnerabilities due to direct string interpolation/concatenation instead of parameterized queries. These vulnerabilities allow attackers to execute arbitrary SQL commands, potentially leading to data breaches, data loss, or complete database compromise. Additionally, searchTodosByStatus has a type mismatch (string instead of boolean), and all functions lack input validation present in existing code. The code violates established secure coding patterns demonstrated in the same file (createTodo, getTodoById, etc.).

testCoverage.summary: Test coverage is severely inadequate at approximately 15%. Only 2 of 11 exported functions have tests (validateTodoInput and sanitizeInput). The three newly added search functions (searchTodos, searchTodosByStatus, getTodosByUser) have ZERO test coverage despite containing critical SQL injection vulnerabilities explicitly marked in comments. These vulnerabilities are the most urgent gaps - tests must demonstrate the injection attacks succeed to document attack vectors for security remediation. Five core CRUD functions (createTodo, getAllTodos, getTodoById, updateTodoStatus, deleteTodo) remain completely untested despite being in production. Existing tests for validation and sanitization have good coverage of their logic but miss boundary conditions (200-char title, 1000-char description) and edge cases (double-escaping, ampersand handling). The test file uses no database mocking, suggesting integration tests may exist elsewhere, but no evidence of their scope was found. Major risks: security vulnerabilities are unverified, core business logic is untested, error paths are not covered, and edge cases like empty inputs, special characters, and type mismatches have no assertions. Immediate action required: add security tests proving SQL injection exists, mock database layer for unit tests of CRUD operations, and cover all error paths before this PR can safely merge.

suggestions.description: Replace SQL string interpolation with parameterized query to match existing secure patterns and prevent SQL injection
suggestions.benefits: Prevents SQL injection attacks by using parameterized queries consistent with getTodoById, updateTodoStatus, deleteTodo, and createTodo. Eliminates a recurring vulnerability pattern that would require fixes across multiple components when security standards evolve.

suggestions.description: Replace string concatenation with parameterized query and add type safety for boolean parameter
suggestions.benefits: Prevents SQL injection via parameterized queries and improves type safety by using boolean instead of string for the completed parameter, matching the Todo interface definition. Aligns with updateTodoStatus which uses boolean for the same field.

suggestions.description: Replace template literal with parameterized query to prevent SQL injection in JOIN statement
suggestions.benefits: Prevents SQL injection in JOIN queries by using parameterized queries consistent with all other database operations in the file. Protects against malicious user IDs that could extract or modify unauthorized data.

suggestions.description: Add input validation for search parameters before database queries
suggestions.benefits: Adds defense-in-depth by validating and sanitizing inputs before queries, matching the pattern used in createTodo. Prevents empty searches and enforces reasonable length limits consistent with the Todo schema validation.

suggestions.description: Rename variable from 'sql' to 'query' for consistency with rest of codebase
suggestions.before: const sql = 'SELECT * FROM todos WHERE completed = $1';
suggestions.after: const query = 'SELECT * FROM todos WHERE completed = $1';
suggestions.benefits: Maintains naming consistency across all database functions. Every other function in the file uses 'query' as the variable name for SQL statements (createTodo, getAllTodos, getTodoById, updateTodoStatus, deleteTodo).

suggestions.description: Extract common result mapping pattern to reduce type assertion duplication
suggestions.before:
const rows = await db.query(query, [searchPattern]);
return rows as Todo[];
suggestions.benefits: Centralizes the type assertion logic in one place. If runtime validation is added later (e.g., using a schema validator like Zod), only one function needs to be updated instead of modifying every query function.

refactorings.summary: The three new search functions introduce SQL injection vulnerabilities through string concatenation and template literals, directly violating the established parameterized query pattern used throughout the codebase. All three functions require immediate pattern-improvement refactoring to use parameterized queries. Additional improvements include type safety (boolean instead of string for completed status), input validation matching createTodo's approach, consistent variable naming, and extracting the common type assertion pattern to enable future runtime validation enhancements.

recommendations.description: All three new functions contain SQL injection vulnerabilities. Immediate action required: Replace string concatenation and template literals with parameterized queries using $1, $2 placeholders and parameter arrays. This is a blocking issue that must be fixed before merge.

Zero test coverage for the three new search functions despite containing critical security vulnerabilities. Add comprehensive tests including security tests that demonstrate SQL injection attacks, edge cases for empty inputs, special characters, and type validation failures.

The searchTodosByStatus function has a type mismatch - the 'completed' parameter is typed as string but should be boolean to match the Todo interface and database schema. Change parameter type from string to boolean.

New search functions lack input validation that is present in existing functions like createTodo. Add validation for empty strings, excessive length, and invalid formats before executing database queries. This provides defense-in-depth security.

New functions violate established patterns in the codebase. All existing database functions (createTodo, getTodoById, updateTodoStatus, deleteTodo) use parameterized queries, input validation, and consistent variable naming. Align new code with these patterns.

The searchTodos function uses leading wildcard LIKE patterns ('%keyword%') which prevent index usage and cause full table scans. Consider implementing full-text search or at least documenting the performance implications for large datasets.
